founderDecisionRecommendations.F1-bara: Ratify 'create' / 'Creator' for all 14 Isaiah sites (overlay bara-create-isaiah). Yes, the Genesis 'shape' should be reviewed at the next Genesis pass. Reasons: (1) the Qal/Niphal never takes an accusative of material and the lexica gloss it 'create' (BDB; HALOT brʾ I; Bernhardt TDOT 2; Schmidt THAT 1). (2) The central bara rationale's 'Piel "cut out, fashion"' is the separate homonym 'cut down, clear (forest)' (Josh 17:15, 18; Ezek 23:47; HALOT). Its '(Gesenius §17)' locator is wrong as a GKC reference, since GKC §17 treats Qere/Ketiv. (3) The central yatsar entry glosses yāṣar 'form, shape, fashion (as a potter)', so 'shape' for bārāʾ already collides with the potter's verb even in Genesis. (4) The canon itself uses 'créés, formés et faits' (Isa 43:7). Corpus finding: AMO-WOH-4:13 already renders bôrēʾ rûaḥ 'shapes the wind', an extension of the Genesis 'shape' outside the central appliesTo that is now inconsistent with Isaiah. Review it together with the Genesis decision. Options for the Genesis review: re-render 'create' and keep the bārāʾ/ʿāśāh/yāṣar distinction as create/make/form (the Isaiah model), or keep 'shape' but downgrade the central entry to speculative with a corrected rationale.

paragraphs.text: וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י גְאַלְתִּ֔יךָ קָרָ֥אתִי בְשִׁמְךָ֖ לִי־אָֽתָּה׃

i18n.en: But now thus says YHWH, who created you, O Jacob, and who formed you, O Israel: Do not fear, for I have redeemed you; I have called you by your name; you are mine.
i18n.he: וְעַתָּ֞ה כֹּֽה־אָמַ֤ר יְהוָה֙ בֹּרַאֲךָ֣ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיֹצֶרְךָ֖ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל אַל־תִּירָא֙ כִּ֣י גְאַלְתִּ֔יךָ קָרָ֥אתִי בְשִׁמְךָ֖ לִי־אָֽתָּה׃

notes.official: *bōrăʾăḵā yaʿăqōḇ wᵉyōṣerḵā yiśrāʾēl* “who created you, O Jacob, and who formed you, O Israel.” Second Isaiah applies the creation verbs to the making of a people. *bārāʾ* is “create” (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`) and *yāṣar* is “form,” the potter’s verb (central `yatsar`). The two participles are rendered as relative clauses, keeping their verbal force, rather than as titles (“your Creator … your Former”). *gᵉʾaltîḵā* “I have redeemed you”: *gāʾal* is the kinsman’s duty to buy back a relative from debt-slavery.

paragraphs.text: כִּֽי־תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּמַּ֙יִם֙ אִתְּךָ־אָ֔נִי וּבַנְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּךָ כִּֽי־תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר־בָּֽךְ׃

i18n.en: When you pass through the waters, I will be with you; and through the rivers, they shall not overflow you; when you walk through fire, you shall not be burned, and the flame shall not consume you.
i18n.he: כִּֽי־תַעֲבֹ֤ר בַּמַּ֙יִם֙ אִתְּךָ־אָ֔נִי וּבַנְּהָר֖וֹת לֹ֣א יִשְׁטְפ֑וּךָ כִּֽי־תֵלֵ֤ךְ בְּמוֹ־אֵשׁ֙ לֹ֣א תִכָּוֶ֔ה וְלֶהָבָ֖ה לֹ֥א תִבְעַר־בָּֽךְ׃

paragraphs.text: כִּ֗י אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ נָתַ֤תִּי כָפְרְךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם כּ֥וּשׁ וּסְבָ֖א תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

i18n.en: For I am YHWH your God, the Holy One of Israel, your Savior; I have given Egypt as your ransom, Cush and Seba instead of you.
i18n.he: כִּ֗י אֲנִי֙ יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֶ֔יךָ קְד֥וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מוֹשִׁיעֶ֑ךָ נָתַ֤תִּי כָפְרְךָ֙ מִצְרַ֔יִם כּ֥וּשׁ וּסְבָ֖א תַּחְתֶּֽיךָ׃

notes.official: *ʾănî YHWH ʾĕlōheyḵā* “I am YHWH your God” (overlay suffixed-*ʾĕlōhîm* pattern). *kûš* is rendered “Cush” (Gen 10:6–8), the Nubian kingdom south of Egypt. ASV and NRSV “Ethiopia” follow the LXX *Aithiopia* but now point to a different country. *taḥteḵā* “instead of you” is the substitution formula, rendered under the central `tachat-substitution-formula` entry, as at 53:12.

paragraphs.text: מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקַ֧רְתָּ בְעֵינַ֛י נִכְבַּ֖דְתָּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֲהַבְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶתֵּ֤ן אָדָם֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

i18n.en: Because you are precious in my eyes, you are honored, and I love you; so I give human beings instead of you, and peoples instead of your life.
i18n.he: מֵאֲשֶׁ֨ר יָקַ֧רְתָּ בְעֵינַ֛י נִכְבַּ֖דְתָּ וַאֲנִ֣י אֲהַבְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֶתֵּ֤ן אָדָם֙ תַּחְתֶּ֔יךָ וּלְאֻמִּ֖ים תַּ֥חַת נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

paragraphs.text: אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃

i18n.en: Do not fear, for I am with you; from the east I will bring your seed, and from the west I will gather you.
i18n.he: אַל־תִּירָ֖א כִּ֣י אִתְּךָ־אָ֑נִי מִמִּזְרָח֙ אָבִ֣יא זַרְעֶ֔ךָ וּמִֽמַּעֲרָ֖ב אֲקַבְּצֶֽךָּ׃

notes.official:
*mim-mizrāḥ … ûmim-maʿărāḇ* “from the east … from the west”; v. 6 adds the north and the south. *zarʿăḵā* “your seed” is “offspring,” the descendants scattered in exile.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes vv. 5–7 (« Je ferai venir ta race de l’orient et d’occident … ceux que j’ai, pour ma gloire, créés, formés et faits ! ») and reads the ingathering as the creation of the State of Israel, which received Jews from the north and the south. In the Hebrew the passage promises the return of the exiles, and the line renders it so. The three creation verbs of v. 7 appear in the line as “created … formed … made,” which is also the canon’s wording.

paragraphs.text: אֹמַ֤ר לַצָּפוֹן֙ תֵּ֔נִי וּלְתֵימָ֖ן אַל־תִּכְלָ֑אִי הָבִ֤יאִי בָנַי֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וּבְנוֹתַ֖י מִקְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

i18n.en: I will say to the north, “Give up!” and to the south, “Do not hold back! Bring my sons from afar, and my daughters from the end of the earth,
i18n.he: אֹמַ֤ר לַצָּפוֹן֙ תֵּ֔נִי וּלְתֵימָ֖ן אַל־תִּכְלָ֑אִי הָבִ֤יאִי בָנַי֙ מֵרָח֔וֹק וּבְנוֹתַ֖י מִקְצֵ֥ה הָאָֽרֶץ׃

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו׃

i18n.en: everyone who is called by my name, whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.”
i18n.he: כֹּ֚ל הַנִּקְרָ֣א בִשְׁמִ֔י וְלִכְבוֹדִ֖י בְּרָאתִ֑יו יְצַרְתִּ֖יו אַף־עֲשִׂיתִֽיו׃

notes.official: *wᵉliḵḇôḏî bᵉrāʾṯîw yᵉṣartîw ʾap̄-ʿăśîṯîw* “whom I have created for my glory, whom I have formed, yes, whom I have made.” All three Hebrew creation verbs occur together, as in the pattern of Gen 1–2: *bārāʾ* “create” (overlay `bara-create-isaiah`), *yāṣar* “form” (central `yatsar`), *ʿāśāh* “make” (central `asah`). Each verb has its own English word, so the reader can see that there are three. The Translator’s draft had “shaped,” extending the Genesis-scoped central `bara` entry; the Editor restores “created,” which is also ASV, NRSV, NJPS and the canon’s own “créés.” The closing quotation mark ends YHWH’s command to the four directions that begins in v. 6.

paragraphs.text: הוֹצִ֥יא עַם־עִוֵּ֖ר וְעֵינַ֣יִם יֵ֑שׁ וְחֵרְשִׁ֖ים וְאָזְנַ֥יִם לָֽמוֹ׃

i18n.en: Bring out the people who are blind, yet have eyes, and the deaf, who have ears!
i18n.he: הוֹצִ֥יא עַם־עִוֵּ֖ר וְעֵינַ֣יִם יֵ֑שׁ וְחֵרְשִׁ֖ים וְאָזְנַ֥יִם לָֽמוֹ׃

notes.official:
*hôṣîʾ ʿam-ʿiwwēr wᵉʿênayim yēš* “Bring out the people who are blind, yet have eyes.” The trial scene of vv. 8–13 opens: Israel, blind and deaf, is still called to testify.

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** The canon quotes vv. 8–9 (« Faites sortir le peuple aveugle, mais qui a des yeux … qu’on entende et que l’on dise : c’est vrai ! ») within its reading of the Bible as a testimony preserved by the Jewish people. The line renders the trial scene as the Hebrew presents it.

paragraphs.text: כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו וְיֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִ֤י בָהֶם֙ יַגִּ֣יד זֹ֔את וְרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻ֑נוּ יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ וְיִצְדָּ֔קוּ וְיִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְיֹאמְר֥וּ אֱמֶֽת׃

i18n.en: Let all the nations be gathered together, and let the peoples be assembled. Who among them can declare this, and make us hear the former things? Let them bring their witnesses, that they may be justified; let them hear and say, “It is true.”
i18n.he: כָּֽל־הַגּוֹיִ֞ם נִקְבְּצ֣וּ יַחְדָּ֗ו וְיֵאָֽסְפוּ֙ לְאֻמִּ֔ים מִ֤י בָהֶם֙ יַגִּ֣יד זֹ֔את וְרִֽאשֹׁנ֖וֹת יַשְׁמִיעֻ֑נוּ יִתְּנ֤וּ עֵֽדֵיהֶם֙ וְיִצְדָּ֔קוּ וְיִשְׁמְע֖וּ וְיֹאמְר֥וּ אֱמֶֽת׃

notes.official: *mî ḇāhem yaggîḏ zōʾṯ* “Who among them can declare this?” The nations are challenged to produce witnesses that their gods foretold “the former things.” *yiṣdāqû* is “be justified,” that is, proved in the right before the court. The canon quotes the verse with v. 8; see the note there.

paragraphs.text: אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְעַבְדִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתִּי לְמַ֣עַן תֵּ֠דְעוּ וְתַאֲמִ֨ינוּ לִ֤י וְתָבִ֙ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא לְפָנַי֙ לֹא־נ֣וֹצַר אֵ֔ל וְאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: You are my witnesses, says YHWH, and my servant whom I have chosen, that you may know and believe me, and understand that I am he. Before me no god was formed, nor shall there be any after me.
i18n.he: אַתֶּ֤ם עֵדַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְעַבְדִּ֖י אֲשֶׁ֣ר בָּחָ֑רְתִּי לְמַ֣עַן תֵּ֠דְעוּ וְתַאֲמִ֨ינוּ לִ֤י וְתָבִ֙ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא לְפָנַי֙ לֹא־נ֣וֹצַר אֵ֔ל וְאַחֲרַ֖י לֹ֥א יִהְיֶֽה׃ (ס)

notes.official:
*ʾattem ʿēḏay nᵉʾum-YHWH* “You are my witnesses, says YHWH.” Three points. (1) *wᵉʿaḇdî ʾăšer bāḥārtî* “and my servant whom I have chosen” is rendered plainly (overlay `eved-servant-identity-isaiah`). (2) *kî-ʾănî hûʾ* “that I am he” is the self-identification formula of Second Isaiah (41:4; 43:13; 46:4; 48:12). The French canon has « que je suis le même » (“that I am the same”); the line keeps the standard “I am he.” (3) *lᵉp̄ānay lōʾ-nôṣar ʾēl* “before me no god was formed.” *nôṣar* is the Niphal of *yāṣar* “form,” the verb used for making idols (44:9–12), so the line has lower-case “god,” with NRSV and NJPS (ASV “no God formed”; overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`).

**Wheel of Heaven reading (reception note, not a translation claim).** *The Book Which Tells the Truth* (ch. 5) quotes vv. 10 and 12–13 (« Vous êtes mes témoins ! … aujourd’hui aussi je suis le même ») and reads “You are my witnesses” as referring to the Jewish people and the Bible as witnesses to the coming of the creators. It applies “today also I am the same” to its own messenger’s day. The line renders *ʾănî hûʾ* by the standard “I am he”; on the temporal phrase of v. 13 see the note there.

paragraphs.text: אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מִבַּלְעָדַ֖י מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

i18n.en: I, I am YHWH, and besides me there is no savior.
i18n.he: אָנֹכִ֥י אָנֹכִ֖י יְהוָ֑ה וְאֵ֥ין מִבַּלְעָדַ֖י מוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

paragraphs.text: אָנֹכִ֞י הִגַּ֤דְתִּי וְהוֹשַׁ֙עְתִּי֙ וְהִשְׁמַ֔עְתִּי וְאֵ֥ין בָּכֶ֖ם זָ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽאֲנִי־אֵֽל׃

i18n.en: I declared and I saved and I proclaimed, and there was no stranger among you; and you are my witnesses, says YHWH, and I am God.
i18n.he: אָנֹכִ֞י הִגַּ֤דְתִּי וְהוֹשַׁ֙עְתִּי֙ וְהִשְׁמַ֔עְתִּי וְאֵ֥ין בָּכֶ֖ם זָ֑ר וְאַתֶּ֥ם עֵדַ֛י נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽאֲנִי־אֵֽל׃

notes.official: *wa-ʾănî-ʾēl* “and I am God”: standalone *ʾēl* is “God” (overlay `elohim-el-eloah-monotheistic-formula-isaiah`). *wᵉʾên bākem zār* “and there was no stranger among you”: no foreign god spoke these things.

paragraphs.text: גַּם־מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּ֑יל אֶפְעַ֖ל וּמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Even since the day was, I am he, and there is none who can deliver from my hand; I act, and who can turn it back?
i18n.he: גַּם־מִיּוֹם֙ אֲנִ֣י ה֔וּא וְאֵ֥ין מִיָּדִ֖י מַצִּ֑יל אֶפְעַ֖ל וּמִ֥י יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃ (ס)

notes.official: *gam-mî-yôm ʾănî hûʾ* is ambiguous. It may look back, “even since the day was, I am he” (ASV; NJPS “ever since day was”), or forward, “henceforth I am he” (NRSV; the LXX has *ap’ archēs* “from the beginning”). The French canon reads it as present (« aujourd’hui aussi je suis le même »). The line keeps ASV’s retrospective reading, which follows the plain sense of *mi-yyôm* “from the day,” and records the forward reading here.

paragraphs.text: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְמַעַנְכֶ֞ם שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי בָבֶ֗לָה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י בָֽרִיחִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וְכַשְׂדִּ֖ים בָּאֳנִיּ֥וֹת רִנָּתָֽם׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel: For your sake I have sent to Babylon, and I will bring them all down as fugitives, and the Chaldeans in the ships of their rejoicing.
i18n.he: כֹּֽה־אָמַ֧ר יְהוָ֛ה גֹּאַלְכֶ֖ם קְד֣וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל לְמַעַנְכֶ֞ם שִׁלַּ֣חְתִּי בָבֶ֗לָה וְהוֹרַדְתִּ֤י בָֽרִיחִים֙ כֻּלָּ֔ם וְכַשְׂדִּ֖ים בָּאֳנִיּ֥וֹת רִנָּתָֽם׃

notes.official: The verse is textually difficult. *bārîḥîm* is “fugitives” (ASV, √*brḥ* “flee”) or “bars” (*bᵉrîḥîm*), as in NRSV (“I will break down all the bars”). *bā-ʾŏniyyôṯ rinnāṯām* is “in the ships of their rejoicing” (ASV), or, with an emendation to *ʾănîyôṯ* “lamentations,” “the shouting of the Chaldeans will be turned to lamentation” (NRSV). The line follows MT with ASV.

paragraphs.text: אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם בּוֹרֵ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מַלְכְּכֶֽם׃ (ס)

i18n.en: I am YHWH, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King.
i18n.he: אֲנִ֥י יְהוָ֖ה קְדֽוֹשְׁכֶ֑ם בּוֹרֵ֥א יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מַלְכְּכֶֽם׃ (ס)

notes.official: *bôrēʾ yiśrāʾēl* “the Creator of Israel”: the participle stands in a series of titles (“your Holy One … your King”) and is rendered as a title (ASV; overlay `bara-create-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם עַזִּ֖ים נְתִיבָֽה׃

i18n.en: Thus says YHWH, who makes a way in the sea, and a path in the mighty waters,
i18n.he: כֹּ֚ה אָמַ֣ר יְהוָ֔ה הַנּוֹתֵ֥ן בַּיָּ֖ם דָּ֑רֶךְ וּבְמַ֥יִם עַזִּ֖ים נְתִיבָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב־וָס֖וּס חַ֣יִל וְעִזּ֑וּז יַחְדָּ֤ו יִשְׁכְּבוּ֙ בַּל־יָק֔וּמוּ דָּעֲכ֖וּ כַּפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה כָבֽוּ׃

i18n.en: who brings out chariot and horse, army and warrior — they lie down together, they shall not rise; they are extinguished, quenched like a wick:
i18n.he: הַמּוֹצִ֥יא רֶֽכֶב־וָס֖וּס חַ֣יִל וְעִזּ֑וּז יַחְדָּ֤ו יִשְׁכְּבוּ֙ בַּל־יָק֔וּמוּ דָּעֲכ֖וּ כַּפִּשְׁתָּ֥ה כָבֽוּ׃

paragraphs.text: אַֽל־תִּזְכְּר֖וּ רִֽאשֹׁנ֑וֹת וְקַדְמֹנִיּ֖וֹת אַל־תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ׃

i18n.en: Do not remember the former things, nor consider the things of old.
i18n.he: אַֽל־תִּזְכְּר֖וּ רִֽאשֹׁנ֑וֹת וְקַדְמֹנִיּ֖וֹת אַל־תִּתְבֹּנָֽנוּ׃

paragraphs.text: הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ עַתָּ֣ה תִצְמָ֔ח הֲל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּהָ אַ֣ף אָשִׂ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֔רֶךְ בִּֽישִׁמ֖וֹן נְהָרֽוֹת׃

i18n.en: Behold, I am doing a new thing; now it springs forth; do you not perceive it? I will make a way in the wilderness, rivers in the desert.
i18n.he: הִנְנִ֨י עֹשֶׂ֤ה חֲדָשָׁה֙ עַתָּ֣ה תִצְמָ֔ח הֲל֖וֹא תֵֽדָע֑וּהָ אַ֣ף אָשִׂ֤ים בַּמִּדְבָּר֙ דֶּ֔רֶךְ בִּֽישִׁמ֖וֹן נְהָרֽוֹת׃

notes.official: *hinnî ʿōśeh ḥăḏāšāh* “Behold, I am doing a new thing.” MT *bîšîmōn nᵉhārôṯ* is “rivers in the desert.” The Great Isaiah Scroll (1QIsaᵃ) reads נתיבות *nᵉṯîḇôṯ* “paths” in v. 19, a closer parallel to *dereḵ* “way,” and keeps “rivers” in v. 20. The line keeps MT (overlay `mt-qere-textual-policy-isaiah`).

paragraphs.text: תְּכַבְּדֵ֙נִי֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה תַּנִּ֖ים וּבְנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה כִּֽי־נָתַ֨תִּי בַמִּדְבָּ֜ר מַ֗יִם נְהָרוֹת֙ בִּֽישִׁימֹ֔ן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת עַמִּ֥י בְחִירִֽי׃

i18n.en: The beasts of the field will honor me, the jackals and the ostriches, because I give water in the wilderness, rivers in the desert, to give drink to my people, my chosen,
i18n.he: תְּכַבְּדֵ֙נִי֙ חַיַּ֣ת הַשָּׂדֶ֔ה תַּנִּ֖ים וּבְנ֣וֹת יַֽעֲנָ֑ה כִּֽי־נָתַ֨תִּי בַמִּדְבָּ֜ר מַ֗יִם נְהָרוֹת֙ בִּֽישִׁימֹ֔ן לְהַשְׁק֖וֹת עַמִּ֥י בְחִירִֽי׃

paragraphs.text: עַם־זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: the people whom I formed for myself, that they might recount my praise.
i18n.he: עַם־זוּ֙ יָצַ֣רְתִּי לִ֔י תְּהִלָּתִ֖י יְסַפֵּֽרוּ׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: וְלֹא־אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־יָגַ֥עְתָּ בִּ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

i18n.en: Yet you did not call upon me, O Jacob; but you have grown weary of me, O Israel.
i18n.he: וְלֹא־אֹתִ֥י קָרָ֖אתָ יַֽעֲקֹ֑ב כִּֽי־יָגַ֥עְתָּ בִּ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

paragraphs.text: לֹֽא־הֵבֵ֤יאתָ לִּי֙ שֵׂ֣ה עֹלֹתֶ֔יךָ וּזְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א כִבַּדְתָּ֑נִי לֹ֤א הֶעֱבַדְתִּ֙יךָ֙ בְּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הוֹגַעְתִּ֖יךָ בִּלְבוֹנָֽה׃

i18n.en: You have not brought me the sheep of your burnt-offerings, nor honored me with your sacrifices; I have not burdened you with meal-offerings, nor wearied you with frankincense.
i18n.he: לֹֽא־הֵבֵ֤יאתָ לִּי֙ שֵׂ֣ה עֹלֹתֶ֔יךָ וּזְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א כִבַּדְתָּ֑נִי לֹ֤א הֶעֱבַדְתִּ֙יךָ֙ בְּמִנְחָ֔ה וְלֹ֥א הוֹגַעְתִּ֖יךָ בִּלְבוֹנָֽה׃

paragraphs.text: לֹא־קָנִ֨יתָ לִּ֤י בַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ קָנֶ֔ה וְחֵ֥לֶב זְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א הִרְוִיתָ֑נִי אַ֗ךְ הֶעֱבַדְתַּ֙נִי֙ בְּחַטֹּאותֶ֔יךָ הוֹגַעְתַּ֖נִי בַּעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃ (ס)

i18n.en: You have not bought me sweet cane with silver, nor sated me with the fat of your sacrifices; but you have burdened me with your sins, you have wearied me with your iniquities.
i18n.he: לֹא־קָנִ֨יתָ לִּ֤י בַכֶּ֙סֶף֙ קָנֶ֔ה וְחֵ֥לֶב זְבָחֶ֖יךָ לֹ֣א הִרְוִיתָ֑נִי אַ֗ךְ הֶעֱבַדְתַּ֙נִי֙ בְּחַטֹּאותֶ֔יךָ הוֹגַעְתַּ֖נִי בַּעֲוֺנֹתֶֽיךָ׃ (ס)

paragraphs.text: אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י ה֛וּא מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ לְמַעֲנִ֑י וְחַטֹּאתֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶזְכֹּֽר׃

i18n.en: I, I am he who blots out your transgressions for my own sake, and I will not remember your sins.
i18n.he: אָנֹכִ֨י אָנֹכִ֥י ה֛וּא מֹחֶ֥ה פְשָׁעֶ֖יךָ לְמַעֲנִ֑י וְחַטֹּאתֶ֖יךָ לֹ֥א אֶזְכֹּֽר׃

paragraphs.text: הַזְכִּירֵ֕נִי נִשָּׁפְטָ֖ה יָ֑חַד סַפֵּ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה לְמַ֥עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃

i18n.en: Remind me; let us go to judgment together; set forth your case, that you may be justified.
i18n.he: הַזְכִּירֵ֕נִי נִשָּׁפְטָ֖ה יָ֑חַד סַפֵּ֥ר אַתָּ֖ה לְמַ֥עַן תִּצְדָּֽק׃

paragraphs.text: אָבִ֥יךָ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן חָטָ֑א וּמְלִיצֶ֖יךָ פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

i18n.en: Your first father sinned, and your teachers transgressed against me.
i18n.he: אָבִ֥יךָ הָרִאשׁ֖וֹן חָטָ֑א וּמְלִיצֶ֖יךָ פָּ֥שְׁעוּ בִֽי׃

notes.official: *ʾāḇîḵā hā-rîšôn* “your first father” is Jacob (cf. Hos 12:3–5) or Abraham. *mᵉlîṣeḵā* “your teachers” (ASV) are, more exactly, “interpreters, spokesmen” (NRSV “your interpreters”), the mediators of the people.

paragraphs.text: וַאֲחַלֵּ֖ל שָׂ֣רֵי קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לַחֵ֙רֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְגִדּוּפִֽים׃ (ס)

i18n.en: Therefore I will profane the princes of the sanctuary, and I will give Jacob to be devoted to destruction, and Israel to revilings.
i18n.he: וַאֲחַלֵּ֖ל שָׂ֣רֵי קֹ֑דֶשׁ וְאֶתְּנָ֤ה לַחֵ֙רֶם֙ יַעֲקֹ֔ב וְיִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל לְגִדּוּפִֽים׃ (ס)

notes.official: *laḥ-ḥērem* “to be devoted to destruction” (central `cherem-devote-to-destruction-cross-corpus`, ratified 2026-11-01: ḥērem is “devote(d) to destruction” across the corpus). *ḥērem* is the sacral ban, total destruction devoted to the deity (Deut 7:2; Josh 6:17; Lohfink, TDOT 5:180–199). ASV’s “curse” confuses it with the words for curse, *ʾālāh* and *qᵉlālāh*; NRSV has “utter destruction” (overlay `lexical-cruxes-wave-i2-isaiah`). The tense is kept future with ASV. The Masoretic *waʾăḥallēl* has the simple *waw* with pataḥ, not the qamets of a narrative past, although NJPS repoints it to “So I profaned … and delivered.”
